1023b29: From these the one is made. For the universal, and what is called 'whole' in the general sense,
1023b30: as being a kind of whole, is thus a universal as containing many by virtue of
1023b31: being predicated of each and all things being one as each,
1023b34: most of all in potentiality, but if not, in actuality. Of these
1023b35: the ones that are such by nature rather than by art are so more truly, just as also
1023b36: we said in the case of the one, since wholeness is a kind of unity.
1024a1: Further, of a quantum that has a beginning and a middle and an end, those
1024a2: in which position makes no difference are called 'all,' while those in which it does make a difference
1024a4: these are things whose nature remains the same upon transposition, but
1024a5: whose shape does not, for instance wax and a garment; for both 'whole' and
1024a6: 'all' are said of them; for they have both. Water and all things liquid,
1024a9: those of which 'all' is said as of a unit, of these 'all' (in the plural) is said as of things divided;
1024a10: all this number, all these units.
